headline: EEI roof, HVAC, and solar contracts for three schools, up to $9.4 million, ended in a 4-4 tie.
summary: Members also approved a $73,075 van for career and technical education (CTE) programs and a $120,780 speech services contract for McCarthy Middle School Alternative Program. They approved policies on special education, religious accommodations, and conduct on school. A special education update covered about 2,175 students with active IEPs.
decisions: Motion to table the discussion of the EEI presentation failed 4-4.
Approved an amendment removing the School Administration Building ($451,750) from the EEI contracts, 7-1.
Motion to approve EEI contracts for three schools, not to exceed $9,414,505.00, failed on a 4-4 tie, though the minutes say it passes.
Approved buying a 15-passenger van from Grappone Ford for CTE programs, not to exceed $73,075.00, 7-0.
Approved a contract with Champion Speech Therapy for speech services at McCarthy Middle School Alternative Program, not to exceed $120,780.00, 7-0.
Approved a contract with BlazerWorks LLC for staffing of 1.0 FTE BT, not to exceed $45,250.00, 7-0.
Approved the FY27 October Transfer Report, 6-0.
Approved Policy ACE, Procedural Safeguards and non-discrimination on the basis of handicap/disability, 6-0.
Approved Policy IHBA, Programs for Pupils with Disabilities, 6-0.
Approved Policy IHBA-R1, Section 504 notice of parent and student rights, 6-0.
Approved Policy IHBAA on criteria for special education evaluations, 6-0.
Approved Policy IHBAB on special education evaluations, 7-0.
Approved Policy ACD on religious neutrality and religious accommodations, 7-0.
Approved Policy KFA, Conduct on School, 7-0.
Approved the November 16, 2026 personnel recommendations, including one nomination and one resignation, 7-0.
Approved the memorandum of understanding with the NTU, Unit A, on the grievance filed by three teachers, 7-0.
Approved two sidebar agreements with the AFSCME Local 365, Council 93 Union, 7-0.

BOARD OF EDUCATION 
MONDAY, NOVEMBER 16, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Board of Education was held at NHS North on Monday, November 16, 2026.  Ms. Bishop 
called the meeting to order at 6:13 pm and asked Ms. Lamphier to read the opening statement and Ms. Lewis 
to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Present: Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Lewis, Mr. Salvi, Ms. Lamphier, Ms. Lopez (6:16 pm), 
and Ms. Bishop 
 
Also Present:  Dr. Andrade, Dr. Scarpati, Mr. O’Rourke, Ms. DeGray, Mr. Smith, Dr. Vicente, Ms. Saad 
(6:45 pm), Ms. Praturu, Mr. Davies (EEI), 
 
Also Present:  Members of the Public, Channel 99 Videographer 
  
PRESENTATIONS:   
EEI:   
• Mr. Smith described a deferred-maintenance backlog of about $14 million and proposed combined roof, 
HVAC, and solar work at Charlotte Avenue, Fairgrounds, and Ledge Street.  The District Administration 
building needs HVAC and possibly solar (new roof installed summer 2026). 
• Board members discussed costs, enrollment and tax concerns, roof leaks, solar savings, rebates, and 
potential city financing. Discussion recommended excluding SAU office from the approved scope. 
• City appropriation and funding remain open; the agreement has a non-appropriation provision. 
 
Ms. Lopez moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis to table the discussion on the EEI presentation by roll call. 
 
• Additional clarification was provided by Mr. Smith and Ms. DeGray on misinformation of solar savings to 
the district. 
 
N Sharon Giglio ab Heather Raymond Y Regan Lamphier 
N Kirsten Prinn Y Jaimeika Lewis Y Shewanda Lopez 
N Rob Johnson Y Santosh Salvi N Jennifer Bishop 
 
Motion fails (4-4). 
 
Ms. Giglio moved to approve entering into contracts with EEI to complete the HVAC/Roofing/Solar projects 
at Charlotte Avenue, Fairgrounds Elementary, Ledge Street Elementary, and the School Administration 
building.  Total project cost is potentially $9,866,255.00. 
 
Ms. Lewis moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to amend the motion by removing the School Administration 
Building (-$451,750) for a new total project cost not to exceed $9,414,505.00. 
 
Y Sharon Giglio ab Heather Raymond Y Regan Lamphier 
Y Kirsten Prinn Y Jaimeika Lewis N Shewanda Lopez 
Y Rob Johnson Y Santosh Salvi Y Jennifer Bishop 
 
Motion Passes 7-1.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  November 16, 2026 
 
 
2 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Bishop, to approve entering into contracts with EEI to complete the 
HVAC/Roofing/Solar projects at Charlotte Avenue, Fairgrounds Elementary, and Ledge Street 
Elementary.  Total project cost not to exceed $9,414,505.00.   
 
Motion passes 4-4 (Nay:  Mr. Johnson, Ms. Lamphier, Mr. Salvi, and Ms. Lopez) 
 
STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE COMMENTS 
• Ms. Praturu:  Nashua High School South Boys Soccer won the NHIA Division 1 Championship with 
an undefeated season. 
• Ms. Saad:  Winter sports start after Thanksgiving. 
 
Special Education Presentation: 
• Dr. Vicente introduced the RISE (resources, inclusion, services and special education) team and shared 
district data, including roughly 2,175 students with active IEPs, about 23% of enrollment, along with state 
indicator results on timely evaluations, age-three readiness, inclusion, early-childhood data, and lower per-
student special-education spending than some NH districts. 
• Discussion covered early-childhood inclusion and enrollment, including Franklin Street’s integrated model, 
the lack of universal pre-K, Title I pre-K, and requested enrollment and waitlist figures; IEP meeting 
efficiency and LEA training, including the three-meeting process and interest in streamlining; identification 
and service transitions, progress monitoring, the continuum of services, and grade-level transitions; 
extracurricular and community participation; intensive-needs staffing and programming; the McCarthy 
Alternative Program’s Constellations partnership and program review; and the proposed Parent Advisory 
Council and December information sessions, with possible additional community locations. 
• Board members asked many clarifying questions during the presentation.   
 
Mr. Salvi left meeting at 8:30 pm 
 
 
CONSENT AGENDA 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the Consent Agenda.  Motion passes 7-0. 
 
ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT AGENDA 
 
COMMUNICATIONS OUTSIDE THE CONSENT AGENDA 
 
PUBLIC QUESTION/COMMENT PERIOD LIMITED TO ITEMS ON THIS AGENDA 
• Stephen Scaer, Nashua:  Policy ACD 
• Beth Scaer, Nashua:  Policy ACD 
• Gary Hoffman, Nashua:  Memorandum of Understanding 
 
SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Congratulations to the Nashua High School South Boys' Soccer Team on capturing the New 
Hampshire State Championship! 
• The NHDOE released its updated school improvement designations. The following Nashua schools 
have been identified: 
 
Additional Targeted Support and Improvement (ATSI) / Targeted Support and Improvement (TSI) 
• Pennichuck Middle School – ATSI (2023) 
• Charlotte Avenue Elementary School – ATSI (2026)
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  November 16, 2026 
 
 
3 
• Ledge Street Elementary School – ATSI/TSI (2026) 
• Fairgrounds Elementary School – ATSI (2026) 
• Birch Hill Elementary School – ATSI (2026) 
 
Comprehensive Support and Improvement (CSI) 
• Dr. Norman W. Crisp Elementary School 
• Brentwood Academy 
• Mt. Pleasant Elementary School 
• Amherst Street Elementary School 
 
• Superintendent Mario Andrade reported the literacy, coaching, staffing, and instructional initiatives to 
help address to designations. 
 
 
BOARD RESPONSE TO SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Board members thank Dr. Vicente and Dr. Andrade for the presentations and data update regarding 
the school designations. 
 
 
COMMITTEE ON BUDGET 
 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND OPERATIONS 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the purchase of a 15-passenger van from 
Grappone Ford for use in the CTE programs in an amount not to exceed $73,075.00.  Funding to come 
from the CTE Special Revenue account.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with Champion Speech Therapy for 
speech services at McCarthy Middle School Alternative Program during the 2026-2027 school year at a 
cost not to exceed $120,780.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Out-of-District 
Tuition.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with BlazerWorks LLC for staffing 
of 1.0 FTE BT for the 2026-2027 school year at a total cost not to exceed $45,250.00. Funding to be 
charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
Ms. Lopez stepped out at 9:10 pm 
 
• Ms. Lamphier noted that $550,000 was transferred from wages into contract services this month. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the FY27 October Transfer Report.   
 
Motion passes 6-0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  November 16, 2026 
 
 
4 
COMMITTEE ON POLICY 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve Policy ACE - Procedural Safeguards - Non-
Discrimination on the Basis of Handicap/Disability.   
 
Motion passes 6-0. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve Policy IHBA - Programs for Pupils with 
Disabilities.   
 
Motion passes 6-0. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve Policy IHBA-R1 - Programs for Pupils with 
Disabilities Section 504 – Notice of Parent & Student Rights.   
 
Motion passes 6-0. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve Policy IHBAA - Criterial for Special 
Education Evaluations.   
 
Motion passes 6-0. 
 
Ms. Lopez returned at 9:15 pm 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve Policy IHBAB - Special Education 
Evaluations.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to approve Policy ACD – Religious Neutrality & 
Religious Accommodations.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Lamphier, to waive the 2nd reading of Policy KFA – Conduct on 
School.   
 
Motion passes 6-1(Nay - Ms. Lopez). 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve Policy KFA – Conduct on School.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
 
COMMITTEE ON HUMAN RESOURCES 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to suspend the rules to consider items from the HR meeting held 
earlier this evening.   
 
Motion passes 7-0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  November 16, 2026 
 
 
5 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the November 16, 2026 Personnel  
Recommendations.   
 
Motion passes 7-0.

UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
 
 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
Ms. Lopez moved, seconded by Ms. Giglio, to approve the MOU between the Board of Education and the 
NTU, Unit A – Teachers, “Resolution to Grievance filed by Amy Arseneault, Crystal Seagle, and Leah 
Fiasconaro-Conway”.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
Ms. Bishop moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the two (2) Sidebar Agreements with the AFSCME 
Local 365, Council 93 Union.   
 
Motion passes 7-0. 
 
 
LIAISON REPORTS 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
• Abby Byrd, Nashua:  Keep schools open – City residents in the south end are older in age and young 
people with children will come back.  Be prepared. 
• Alex Homola, 6 Ayers Street, Nashua:  Shared great events and volunteers at Mt. Pleasant:  Girls on 
the Run did a 5K in Concord; shout out to the coaches who volunteer their time; 35 families will be 
provided Thanksgiving dinners through the generosity of PTO, counselors and family engagement 
coordinator. 
 
 
BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS 
None 
 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to adjourn.  So voted at 9:43 pm. 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
